rationale: Evidence: all 60 development trials went off track (0 finishes). Progress was only 0.11 to 0.15, with one line-loss event per run and max_error about 0.062 m, just above the 0.06 m off-track limit. The body-width term cannot raise that limit above 0.0575 m within the allowed body range, so the fix has to come from tracking error, not from a wider body. The robot is losing the line early and drifting out. Likely causes: kp 2.5 with base_speed 1.6 is too aggressive (large PWM swings on each unit of signal, so it overshoots and oscillates); the sensor array spans only +/-0.03 m, so once the line moves past the outer sensors the robot is blind; and kd 0.15 gives little damping. Changes: (1) kp 2.5 to 1.6 to reduce overshoot; (2) kd 0.15 to 0.4 to damp oscillation; (3) base_speed 1.6 to 1.4 so there is more time to correct on bends, at some cost to finish time; (4) sensor spread widened to +/-0.045 m (five sensors at x = -0.045, -0.0225, 0, 0.0225, 0.045, y = 0.04) so the line stays visible at larger lateral error; (5) mass 0.8 to 0.6 kg to lower yaw inertia and speed up correction; (6) ki kept at 0.05. Expected result: fewer line-loss events and max_error below 0.06 m on the oval and s-bend, with completion possible on at least some seeds. Hypotheses: H1, the line is lost from the sensor edge during the first bends, not from noise; H2, kp is the main source of oscillation. Measurements wanted next: completion_time and progress to see whether speed or steering limits the finish, max_error and line_loss_events to see whether the sensor spread fixed the blind spot, and steering_oscillation to test H2.
